replies.author: @GeckoHiker
replies.text:
I bake cookies from scratch with ingredients I acquired in bulk or at deep discount. My grocery budget is $60 a month for two adults, and we technically don't need to shop anymore. We also have chickens and a garden, which is part of our budgeting strategy. I started an indoor garden for scallions, celery, herbs, and greens several years ago. I refuse to buy corporate manufactured faux-foods. I buy one-ingredient staples and manufacture my own food. 

I stop in Aldi and Kroger for bargains, like the free potatoes and lemons I picked up yesterday with "best customer" coupons. A package of tilapia was marked down to $2.49 and I had a $1 coupon, so $1.49 for fish that will make up two meals. I grow spinach and will sauté a big mess of greens with lemon juice, butter, and olive oil. California Ranch domestic EVOO was $15.99 on sale for $13.99 and I had a $2 coupon. Popped that bottle in the refrigerator with the others because the olive oil industry is under pressure worldwide. We use olive oil to make marinades, vinaigrettes, and herbed oil for serving steamed or sautéed vegetables.
